status: ILLUSTRATIVE LENS, NOT A DEFAULT ALLOCATION. One probe's weights, chosen to make the flow visible. Nobody has adopted it; every number below is a claim a person would author, contest and replace.
method: Each node splits only its own inbox, once per settlement window, under this lens. Positional share (the land-like part) goes to the node's tier commons; the node's makers keep their labour share; the rest splits equally across the node's direct reliances. A split smaller than the precision floor is not sent: it pools, with its descent recorded, at the tier commons of the node that would have sent it. Each tier keeps a share for its own care and passes the rest to its parent tier. Every split's ratios sum to exactly 1 and each ratio names its reason; a node with no recorded reliance sends its 'rests on' share to its tier commons as unexplained, with descent.

entry.why: The work the money was given for keeps half for the people who made it; half honours what it rests on.

upstream.why: Each upstream keeps most of what reaches it for its own makers and passes a quarter to what it rests on, so the flow thins geometrically with depth. A leaf (no recorded reliance) keeps the same labour share; its quarter is unexplained and pools at the tier commons.

split_rule.why: Equal across direct reliances makes the fewest valuation claims: the lockfile records that a crate is relied on, not how much. The honest weight is 'how the work relies on it', which no record carries yet. Equal invites splitting one project into many crates; grouping by presence (upstream project) is the fix, and the lockfile does not name projects.

positional_share.why: A stand-in for the land-like part of what reaches a node: value it receives because many works clustered around it (a standard everyone relies on), not because of more labour. Fan-in is read from the reverse-index rollup of this one lockfile, a local and partial reading of a community-wide fact. At most a fifth; half of that cap at 20 dependents.

precision_floor.why: One cent: below it a money split cannot be settled, and the record cannot honestly say whose labour it is. Sub-floor shares are not land; they are labour that costs more to attribute than it is worth, held at the tier commons with descent so a finer lens can re-attribute them later.
